# reglobal

> CLI that reinstalls the global npm packages from one Node version into another, for example after `fnm use 26`. Use it when a user has switched or upgraded Node and their global commands are missing, instead of listing and installing them yourself. Install: `npm install -g reglobal`, or `npx reglobal`. Node >= 22, no dependencies.

Work in progress: `export` and `import` are not built yet.

## Workflow

1. Switch to the new Node version first (`fnm use 26`, `nvm use 26`, ...). reglobal installs into the Node that runs it.
2. Preview: `reglobal --dry-run --json` (add `--from 24` to name the old version). Nothing is installed and nothing is asked.
3. Show the user the `plan` and every entry in `warnings`, and get their agreement.
4. Install: the same command with `--yes` in place of `--dry-run`. Check `installed` and `failed` in the JSON.

Do not pipe `y` into the prompt: use `--yes`. Without `--yes`, with `--json` or with no terminal, reglobal installs nothing and exits 1 (`NEEDS_YES`).

## Options

- `--from <version|path>`: the old Node version. `24`, `24.1` or `24.1.0` picks the newest installed match (a leading `v` is fine). A path is that version's install folder or its global `node_modules`. Default: the newest installed version other than the one running.
- `--dry-run`: show the plan, install nothing.
- `--yes` (`-y`): install without asking.
- `--keep-versions`: install the versions the old Node had (`typescript@5.4.0`), and git packages at the same commit. Default: `@latest`, and the latest commit.
- `--list`: compare the old version's globals with this one's, read-only. Does not take `--dry-run`, `--yes` or `--keep-versions`.
- `--json`: JSON on stdout. npm's own output, and without `--json` the `WARNING:` lines, go to stderr.

Versions are found by reading folders, never by running the old Node or npm: fnm (`FNM_DIR`, or its default folder), nvm (`NVM_DIR`, `~/.nvm`), nvm-windows (`NVM_HOME`), mise (`MISE_DATA_DIR`), asdf (`ASDF_DATA_DIR`, `~/.asdf`) and n (`N_PREFIX`, `/usr/local`). For anything else, pass `--from <path>`. The current Node's globals are in the npm prefix (`npm_config_prefix`), or next to `node`.

Installing is one `npm install --global -- <specs>` run by the current Node with its own npm (`npm-cli.js` next to `node`, or the first on PATH), never through a shell. `REGLOBAL_NPM_CLI=<path to npm-cli.js>` picks another.

## JSON

`--list --json`:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "command": "list",
  "from": { "version": "24.3.0", "manager": "fnm", "dir": "/home/me/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v24.3.0/installation/lib/node_modules" },
  "to": { "version": "26.1.0", "dir": "/home/me/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v26.1.0/installation/lib/node_modules" },
  "packages": [
    { "name": "typescript", "version": "5.4.0", "source": "registry", "status": "install" },
    { "name": "cowsay", "version": "1.6.0", "source": "registry", "status": "present", "currentVersion": "1.7.0" },
    { "name": "npm", "version": "10.0.0", "source": "registry", "status": "skipped", "currentVersion": "11.0.0" },
    { "name": "my-tool", "version": "0.1.0", "status": "linked", "link": "/home/me/src/my-tool" }
  ],
  "summary": { "install": 1, "present": 1, "skipped": 1, "linked": 1, "manual": 0, "broken": 0 },
  "warnings": ["my-tool is an npm link to /home/me/src/my-tool: not reinstalled. Run npm link again in that folder."]
}
```

- `status`: `install` (missing here), `present` (already here; `currentVersion` is this one's), `skipped` (npm and corepack come with Node), `linked` (an `npm link`: never installed), `manual` (installed from a local file: install it again by hand), `broken` (no readable package.json).
- `source`: `registry`, `git`, `file` or `url`; anything but `registry` also has `resolved`. Taken from npm's `node_modules/.package-lock.json` or the package's `_resolved`, and `registry` when neither says.
- `from.manager` and `from.version` are `null` when `--from` was a path they can't be read from.

Installing (`--dry-run --json`, `--yes --json`) prints the same fields, with `"command": "install"` and:

```json
{
  "dryRun": false,
  "keepVersions": false,
  "plan": [{ "name": "typescript", "version": "5.4.0", "source": "registry", "spec": "typescript@latest" }],
  "npmExitCode": 0,
  "installed": ["typescript"],
  "failed": []
}
```

`npmExitCode`, `installed` and `failed` are only there after npm ran. A package counts as installed when its folder is in this Node's globals afterwards. On failure the same object also has `error`.

Errors, with `--json`, are on stdout: `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "error": { "code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "..." } }`. Codes: `NO_OLD_VERSION`, `NOT_FOUND`, `BAD_FROM`, `NEEDS_YES`, `NO_NPM`, `INSTALL_FAILED`, `UNKNOWN_OPTION`, `UNKNOWN_COMMAND`, `BAD_OPTION`.

## Exit codes

- `0`: installed everything in the plan, or a dry run or list was shown.
- `1`: error: no old version, npm failed or left a package out, or `--yes` was needed.
- `2`: nothing to install (also from `--dry-run`): not an error.
- `3`: cancelled at the prompt.
